A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TC–RAG and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained experiments and theoretical material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original medical QA experiments, component ablations, threshold-sensitivity results, and appendix noise-attack experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains the medical experiments and reports additional general-domain benchmark results, efficiency measurements, and reasoning trajectories.

M1.justification: V2 adds an explicit Plan action to the action set, prompt, and Algorithm 1. Section 5.3 introduces decoder-stage retrieval/interaction and speculative sampling using a fine-tuned 1.5B draft model. These additions change the action space and inference procedure while retaining the original stack and state-monitor framework.

E1.justification: V2 adds general-domain evaluation on 2WikiMultihopQA and HotpotQA for multihop reasoning, IIRC for reading comprehension, and StrategyQA for commonsense reasoning. The three medical benchmarks and medical pretraining corpus are retained. Appendix 8.8.1 therefore substantially broadens evaluated task and domain coverage.

E2.justification: The twelve medical comparison methods in Table 1 and the CMB leaderboard comparators are unchanged. However, Appendix 8.8.4 expands the original CVP case comparison beyond ReACT by reporting Base, FLARE, and DRAGIN outputs. The general-domain table uses methods already present in v1.

E3.justification: The new general-domain evaluations use Llama3.2-1B, Llama3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B/14B with a common Wiki repository and answer EM/token F1 metrics. Section 6.4 adds interaction, retrieval, latency, and token measurements on Qwen-32B/CMB-Exam. Previously stated medical training budgets, generation settings, and thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds efficiency analysis, expanded CVP reasoning trajectories, and a CMB case demonstrating successive backtracking operations. It removes v1 Section 6.5 and Figure 3's threshold-sensitivity study. The original component ablations and noise-attack analysis remain, and the original ReACT case study moves to Appendix 8.8.3.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and empirical frequencies without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's additional averages and theoretical uncertainty discussion do not introduce experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds efficiency results, including 50.91 seconds for TC–RAG in Table 2, and four-benchmark/four-backbone results in Table 4. These are new evaluations rather than same-setting improvements over v1. Results include exceptions: Llama3.2-1B IIRC EM is 0.066 for TC–RAG versus 0.085 for SR-RAG. Existing medical, noise-attack, and leaderboard scores are unchanged; the gain row and sensitivity curves are removed.

T1.justification: Section 4 and new Appendix 8.3 add Action Validity and state-history assumptions, a mutual-information derivation, a Lyapunov function, and a conditional finite-time convergence theorem with time bounds. V2 also explicitly defines infinite stack memory and bounded state values. The original Turing-machine simulation argument is largely retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list broaden the empirical claim from three medical datasets to seven medical and general-domain datasets. Section 6.2 adds a claim of generalization across domains, tasks, languages, model sizes, and model types. The first-Turing-complete-RAG claim and 7.20% headline remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations for stack selection, the assumption that filtering keeps noise near the stack top, and sequential correction of deeper errors. It adds interpretations of efficiency and generalization results, plus explicit limitations concerning computational cost, scalability, and specialized medical applications. The original threshold-tradeoff interpretation disappears with the sensitivity study.

D1.justification: V2 changes the stated code/data location from SAMA to TC-RAG and explicitly includes RAG resources. It discloses the draft-model size and regex/template parsing with bounded retries in Appendix 8.9. Existing pretraining hardware, duration, learning rates, document chunking, and retriever settings remain unchanged; resource availability is not independently established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for the new benchmarks, decoder interleaving, speculative decoding, and information-theoretic reasoning. It connects its theoretical discussion to Pérez et al.'s Transformer Turing-completeness work and its exception handling to agent frameworks such as AutoGPT. The main RAG taxonomy and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Much of the introduction, related work, method description, and medical-results discussion is retained. V2 updates the author/affiliation block, adds explanatory passages and subheadings, moves the original case study into the appendix, and reorganizes the experimental narrative around efficiency. These are localized editorial and organizational changes.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned with an overall pipeline, state-monitor display, tool library, action diagrams, and worked example. V2 adds efficiency and general-domain result tables, relocates Figure 2 to the appendix, removes Figure 3, and restructures Table 1 by shortening headers and dropping its performance-gain row. Document typography and table formatting also change.

improvement.justification: The new general-domain evaluations and time/token measurements make applicability and practical costs better supported, while limitations and error-handling details improve transparency. These gains are partly offset by removal of the threshold-sensitivity study and generalization language broader than several Table 4 results support. The new convergence guarantee remains conditional on assumed per-step progress. Together, the changes provide a limited net quality improvement.
